metric.why: A hall can be full by power and half empty by space, or the reverse. Tracking both per cabinet is how operators find capacity they already own before building more.
metric.metric: Stranded power and space per cabinet
metric.definition: Utility power or floor space that is allocated and paid for but cannot be used, because the other of the pair ran out first or airflow limits were reached.

reading.body:
Data center operators track stranded power and space per cabinet to identify unused capacity within existing buildings before constructing new facilities, since power and floor space run out independently of each other.

A cabinet may have available electrical supply but lack physical floor space, or possess open floor space while power infrastructure is exhausted. Airflow constraints can strand both resources simultaneously. This metric matters because it separates real capacity constraints from accounting constraints, and because new data center construction is bottlenecked by buildings and power infrastructure. If operators cannot see which resource is the actual limiter in each location, they build when they could have repurposed what exists.

The measurement tracks operational reality rather than nameplate specs. It assumes operators already know their total power and space budgets and reveals only the gap between allocation and usable capacity. This data does not measure utilization rates themselves, the efficiency of cooling systems, or why stranding occurs in specific cases.
